lead.headline: FEDERAL WATCHDOGS PROBE MUSK’S GOLDEN CYBERCAB LAUNCH
lead.summary: Uncle Sam is turning up the heat on Elon Musk's self-driving dreams. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched an official audit query into Tesla's newly debuted steering-wheel-free Cybercab. Regulators are demanding hard technical data on how the electric vehicle giant certified the safety of its autonomous fleet. The sudden federal scrutiny sent shockwaves through Wall Street, putting a damper on the highly anticipated vehicle launch.

stories.headline: Blind Passenger Tests Tesla’s Steering-Wheel-Free Robotaxi
stories.summary: Gary Moss, a man who lost his sight five years ago, took a spin in Tesla's futuristic, steering-wheel-free robotaxi. While Moss described the journey as a comfortable glimpse into regaining his personal independence, he noted the system is still far from perfect. The test highlights the immense, life-changing potential of autonomous vehicles for disabled passengers.

stories.headline: Cosmic Solar Storms Threaten To Crash Autonomous Cars
stories.summary: Scientists warn that threats from deep space could bring self-driving fleets to a grinding halt. A retrospective look at a November 2025 solar storm reveals that celestial disruptions can interfere with vehicle sensors and potentially cause catastrophic crashes. The findings suggest that developers must look to the skies to truly secure the safety of autonomous transit on Earth.

stories.headline: Google and Detroit Clash Over Driverless Future
stories.summary: A fierce battle of philosophies is brewing in the race to conquer the driverless frontier. While tech titan Google pushes for immediate, fully autonomous systems, traditional car manufacturers are taking a slow, incremental approach. Industry experts warn this divergent split could delay safety standards and leave consumers caught in the middle.

stories.headline: Congress Seeks Single Federal Rulebook for Self-Driving Cars
stories.summary: House Republicans are pushing a new draft bill designed to strip local municipalities of their regulatory teeth over self-driving vehicles. The proposed legislation would establish a singular, federal standard for autonomous driving, preventing states and cities from passing their own patchwork safety laws. Proponents argue the move will accelerate innovation, while critics fear a loss of local safety oversight.

stories.headline: India Gets New Baleno Hatchback Packed With Level 2 ADAS
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki has officially launched its updated Baleno hatchback in the competitive Indian market, starting at a modest ₹6.09 lakh. The refreshed model boasts a new Z12E petrol engine and Level 2 advanced driver-assistance systems to tempt safety-minded buyers. The automotive giant is betting big on premium features to capture a larger share of the surging domestic hatchback segment.

lead.headline: OPENAI APOLOGIZES FOR MESSY GPT-6 ASTRA ROLLOUT DELAYS
lead.summary: OpenAI is eating humble pie today after a chaotic rollout of its brand-new GPT-6 Astra model left high-paying customers out in the cold. The tech pioneer issued a formal apology to users who faced massive access delays despite shelling out top dollar for the service. While the firm promises Astra delivers revolutionary advances in coding and computer automation, the launch has been severely bruised by technical bottlenecks. This latest stumble highlights the immense strain on artificial intelligence infrastructure as rivals race for dominance.

stories.headline: Tech Giants Projected to Spend $1.3 Trillion on AI Capex
stories.summary: Six tech behemoths driving the modern artificial intelligence boom are on track to spend a staggering $1.3 trillion on capital expenditures by 2027. Yet, financial analysts warn that only one of these high-spending hyperscalers is projected to maintain a positive free cash flow. This massive spending spree raises serious questions about the long-term profitability of the current silicon gold rush.

stories.headline: New York and Los Angeles Ban AI in Classroom Crackdown
stories.summary: The country's two largest school districts, New York City and Los Angeles, are kicking off the academic year with a strict crackdown on artificial intelligence. Under the new guidelines, students will be barred from using generative AI tools for the vast majority of classroom assignments. The rules highlight a growing national anxiety over academic integrity and the rapid intrusion of automated tech into youth education.

stories.headline: OpenAI Executive Buys Lakeside Camp to Save Bald Eagles
stories.summary: OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman and his wife Anna have put up $5.5 million to purchase a historic 63-acre shoreline property at Big Bear Lake. The generous gift effectively blocks a planned 50-home marina development, preserving a critical nesting ground for bald eagles. The saved habitat is home to the famous Jackie and Shadow eagles, whose livestreamed lives have captivated millions of viewers worldwide.

stories.headline: Seoul Forum Asks if AI Can Speed Up Drug Discovery
stories.summary: A prestigious global forum in Seoul is set to gather top tech executives to tackle one of medicine's greatest challenges: shortening drug development timelines. Experts will investigate whether artificial intelligence can shave an entire decade off the traditional, painstakingly slow process of bringing new therapies to market. The event will also explore AI's disruptive footprint across architecture, art, and entertainment.

stories.headline: Billionaires Launch Ad Campaign to Defend AI Data Centers
stories.summary: A coalition of tech billionaires is pouring massive sums of cash into a new public relations blitz defending controversial AI data centers. The high-priced advertisement campaigns seek to counter growing local opposition and convince skeptical communities that massive computing hubs are vital for America's economic future. Industry leaders argue that the stakes are too high to allow critical infrastructure to be derailed by public backlash.

stories.headline: AI Infrastructure Costs Threaten to Drive Up iPhone Prices
stories.summary: Consumer electronics may soon feel the pinch of "AI inflation" as skyrocketing infrastructure costs hit manufacturing supply chains. Analysts warn that Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 lineup could see significant price hikes as a direct result of surging demand for specialized artificial intelligence hardware. The trend suggests that the costly race to build out global AI networks will ultimately be paid for by everyday shoppers.
